theater: 尼羅河三角洲與佩盧修姆

battle.name: 第三次神聖戰爭
battle.theater: 尼羅河三角洲與佩盧修姆
battle.brief: 公元前356年，阿契美尼德波斯第二次大舉進攻埃及，戰線落在尼羅河三角洲。埃及王阿瑪西斯二世以受希臘式操練的步兵在孟斐斯以北迎敵，並以石料木料封住佩盧修姆的河口，擋下波斯艦隊。卡面的埃及長矛正是這支部隊的主兵器：寬刃青銅矛頭在密集隊形中抵住波斯戰車與弓手，兩次入侵因此無功而還。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 第三次神聖戰爭（公元前356年至前323年）發生在阿契美尼德波斯帝國與埃及第二十六王朝之間，交戰重心在尼羅河三角洲與佩盧修姆一線。波斯方面是中央集權的行省體制：國王阿塔薛西斯二世自居最高統帥，敘利亞—腓尼基、呂底亞等西部行省的總督分掌軍政，前線部隊由各行省徵召的步兵、弓手、重裝戰車與萬人「不死軍」組成，海上投送倚靠腓尼基與塞浦路斯船隊提供的戰船與運輸船。埃及方面是薩易王朝的君主國：法老阿瑪西斯二世在孟斐斯親統軍隊，王室以受雇於埃及的卡里亞人與愛奧尼亞人傭兵團為傳統主力，阿瑪西斯則逐步以受希臘式操練的埃及步兵取代外來傭兵，並從三角洲各州徵召兵員，另有雅典與斯巴達各派來的一支百人重裝步兵小隊。兩邊的指揮系統一為「王—總督—行省部隊」的分層樞紐，一為「法老—王室將官—州徵召兵與傭兵團」的直轄體系，後者反應更快，是埃及能連續化解遠征的制度原因之一。
countriesEn: The Third Sacred War (356–323 BC) was fought between the Achaemenid Persian Empire and Egypt's Twenty-Sixth Dynasty, with the fighting centred on the Nile Delta and the line of Pelusium. On the Persian side stood a centralised satrapal system: King Artaxerxes II was supreme commander, the satraps of the western provinces such as Syria-Phoenicia and Lydia held both military and civil authority, and the field armies were drawn from the levies of the provinces — infantry, archers, armoured chariots and the Immortals — while the sea lift depended on the war galleys and transports supplied by the Phoenician and Cypriot squadrons. On the Egyptian side stood the monarchic state of the Saite dynasty: Pharaoh Amasis II commanded in person from Memphis; the crown had long relied on Carian and Ionian mercenary regiments, and Amasis gradually replaced them with native Egyptian infantry drilled in Greek fashion, drawing recruits from the nomes of the delta, with a further hundred hoplites sent each by Athens and Sparta. The two command systems differed in kind: Persia ran the war through a chain of king, satrap and provincial contingents, while Egypt used the direct route of pharaoh, royal commanders, nome levies and mercenary companies. The latter could react faster, and it was one of the institutional reasons Egypt managed to parry both invasions.
people: 法老阿瑪西斯二世（阿摩西斯二世，約公元前570年至前526年在位）是本戰爭的關鍵人物。他並非出身於薩易王室：他的母親塔舍爾妮塞特原是王室女性，父親是軍人，他本人以軍隊統帥的身分掌握實權，藉阿普里斯的軍隊在賽義德與希拉利翁一線的敗亡奪得王位。即位後他重整軍制、倚重希臘傭兵與希臘商人，使埃及的國庫與三角洲農業同時恢復；本戰爭中每一次波斯遠征都由他應對，他先以外交手段買通波斯統帥，再在第二次遠征時改為以軍力正面決戰。波斯國王阿塔薛西斯二世（約公元前404年至前358年在位）是對手方的決策者，他在位時波斯正忙於塞浦路斯與西頓方向的戰事，仍先後兩次出兵埃及。斯巴達王阿格西勞斯二世與雅典將軍梅涅斯特勞斯率領的重裝步兵，是埃及向希臘城邦求援得到的實際援助；阿格西勞斯在埃及停留後被波斯方面要求召回，返程途中卒於墨加里斯的西爾凱亞（約公元前360年），希臘人把這次合作視為對波斯壓力的第一次牽制。主要史料是公元一世紀的狄奧多羅斯·西庫路斯，其敘事壓縮了年代，學界至今對傭兵到場與戰役先後的排列仍有爭議。戰爭之後接手的波斯國王阿塔薛西斯三世與埃及法老奈克塔內波二世，則分別在第四次神聖戰爭中收復與失去埃及。
peopleEn: Pharaoh Amasis II (Ahmose II, r. c. 570–526 BC) is the decisive figure of this war. He did not come from the Saite royal house: his mother Tashereniset was a woman of the royal family, his father was a soldier, and Amasis himself rose as a commander, taking the throne after Apries' army was broken on the Sais–Heracleion line. Once king he reformed the army, leaned on Greek mercenaries and Greek merchants, and restored the treasury and the agriculture of the delta at the same time. Every Persian expedition in this war was answered by him: he first bought off the Persian commander by diplomacy, and on the second expedition he chose to meet the enemy in the field. The Persian king Artaxerxes II (r. c. 404–358 BC) was the decision-maker on the other side; while his empire was still busy with the wars in the Cyprus and Sidon directions, he nevertheless dispatched two invasions of Egypt. The hoplites led by the Spartan king Agesilaus II and the Athenian general Menestheus were the aid Egypt actually obtained from the Greek cities; after his stay in Egypt Agesilaus was recalled at Persian insistence and died on the road back at Circaea in Megaris (c. 360 BC), and the Greeks counted the episode as their first check on Persian pressure. The principal source is Diodorus Siculus, writing in the first century AD; his narrative compresses the chronology, and scholars still debate the ordering of the mercenaries' arrival and the campaigns themselves. Artaxerxes III, who followed Artaxerxes II, and the Egyptian pharaoh Nectanebo II each took Egypt in the Fourth Sacred War — the former winning it back, the latter losing it.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛被定在早王朝時期，是綁在木杆上的銅或青銅矛頭，是埃及軍械中最古老也最長久的冷兵器。到本次戰爭時代，埃及步兵所用的仍是同一類長矛，只是刃形由早王朝的窄葉變得更寬、更有中脊，杆身為木質、長度在兩米上下，另備短劍作為近身的最後手段。持矛方式與隊形綁在一起：矛握在右手中段、左手托盾，重裝兵在密集方陣裡把矛平伸向前，後排士兵把矛架在前排肩上，整個陣面因此是一片朝前的矛尖，專門用來頂住波斯戰車的衝撞與波斯弓手的近身放箭。埃及一方另有圓盾、短弓、斧，以及用於封堵佩盧修姆河口的石堆與木料；波斯方面的裝備以藤編盾牌、短複合弓、斧頭與標槍為主，並備有阿契美尼德式的重裝戰車與可拋出石塊及箭矢的攻城投擲器材。來援的希臘重裝步兵裝備成制：圓面盾（aspis）、短劍、多里克式頭盔、青銅胸甲與護脛，另配一根較短的長矛。運力方面，埃及靠尼羅河船隊輸送軍糧，波斯遠征軍則倚賴海運船隊與陸路縱隊同行，所有糧秣都得從小亞細亞與敘利亞前線逐段運來。
kitsEn: The card's Egyptian spear is dated to the Early Dynastic period: a copper or bronze head bound to a wooden shaft, the oldest and most durable cold weapon in Egypt's armoury. By the time of this war the Egyptian infantry still carried the same kind of spear, though the blade had widened from the narrow early form into a broader, more ribbed shape; the shaft was wooden and roughly two metres long, and a short sword was carried as the last resort at close quarters. How the spear was held was bound to how the formation fought: gripped at mid-shaft in the right hand with the shield braced in the left, the heavy troops in the dense phalanx levelled the points forward while the rear ranks rested their shafts on the shoulders of the men in front. The face of the formation thus became a bank of forward-thrust points, made for stopping the charge of Persian chariots and the close-range shooting of Persian archers. The Egyptians also used round shields, short bows and axes, together with the stone and timber used to plug the mouths of the Nile at Pelusium; Persian equipment was chiefly wicker shields, short composite bows, axes and javelins, supplemented by Achaemenid heavy chariots and stone- and arrow-throwing artillery. The Greek hoplites who came as reinforcement were equipped to a uniform: the round aspis, a short sword, a Doric helmet, a bronze cuirass and greaves, with a shorter spear of their own. On the logistics side, Egypt moved its rations by boat along the Nile, whereas the Persian expedition depended on its fleet and on its marching columns moving together, and every grain and every order had to come up step by step from Asia Minor and the Syrian front.
tactics: 埃及在這場戰爭裡的戰術核心，是不與波斯在開闊地硬拼，改用三角洲的縱深與水路的控制把遠征軍拖垮。第一次遠征尚未接觸，埃及方面先以巨額金錢買通波斯統帥，讓遠征軍在境內即行折返，避開了正面會戰的風險。第二次遠征則採三層應對：其一，孟斐斯與三角洲各要點築城固守，把城防與河渠交織的縱深交給守軍；其二，主力部隊在三角洲中段的開闊地列成方陣，等波斯軍自東面進入平原之後，以長矛陣面與希臘重裝步兵的圓盾線迎住戰車衝鋒，再用兩翼的埃及步兵與弓手切斷其側後；其三，在佩盧修姆以石料與木料封住尼羅河口的通航水道，使波斯艦隊無法駛入河口登岸，遠征軍只能沿海岸北撤，糧秣與指揮系統被拉成兩段。糧秣方面，埃及全境以尼羅河航運為主幹，軍隊沿河列陣、由河谷供給稻米與魚乾，進退不依賴長距離陸運；波斯軍則要海船與陸隊同行，任何一次登岸失敗都會立刻拉長補給線。
tacticsEn: The tactical core of Egypt's performance in this war was to refuse a set-piece collision with the Persians in open ground and instead use the depth of the delta and control of the water to wear the expedition down. The first invasion was ended before contact: Egypt bought off the Persian commander with a great sum of money, so that the expedition turned back inside Egyptian territory and the risk of a general engagement was avoided altogether. The second invasion was met with a three-part scheme. First, Memphis and the strongpoints of the delta were fortified, leaving the defence of the city lines and the network of canals to the garrisons. Second, the main force drew up in a phalanx in the open ground in the middle of the delta, let the Persian army advance into the plain from the east, met the charge of the chariots with a wall of spears and the round shields of the Greek hoplites, and then swung the Egyptian infantry and archers round to cut the Persian line behind. Third, the mouths of the Nile at Pelusium were plugged with stone and timber so that the Persian fleet could not sail in and land; the expedition had to withdraw northward along the coast, its supply line and its chain of command stretched in two. On rations, the whole of Egypt ran on the Nile as its artery, the army arrayed along the river and fed from the valley with rice and dried fish, so that advance and withdrawal did not depend on long land hauls; the Persian army, by contrast, had to move ships and columns together, and every failure to land cost it immediately in supply.
data: 關於兵力的可靠數字極少，可以確定的部分如下。年代上，第三次神聖戰爭的戰事主要落在公元前358年與公元前356年，常見的編年把整場戰爭的結束定在公元前323年。船隊方面，狄奧多羅斯記載波斯遠征軍備有約二百艘船，另有大量運輸船隨行；希臘援軍的規模則明確：雅典與斯巴達各派一百名重裝步兵。地理上，佩盧修姆到孟斐斯的直線距離約一百六十公里，沿尼羅河支流航行要更久；尼羅河三角洲南北長約兩百公里、東西寬約一百五十公里，任何一支遠征縱隊都要在這樣的三角洲裡拉上好幾天才能展開。作戰上，希羅多德筆下波斯軍的骨幹是萬人「不死軍」，但它在埃及戰役中的實際投入數字沒有留下記錄；波斯與埃及雙方的傷亡人數同樣沒有可信的數字可以引用，本卡因此不列戰損比。唯一可以量化的勝負，是狄奧多羅斯記載的封河動作：埃及人以石料與木料堵住佩盧修姆的河口通道，把波斯艦隊擋在三角洲之外。
dataEn: Reliable figures are scarce, and what can be fixed is as follows. In time, the fighting of the Third Sacred War belongs to 358 and 356 BC, while the usual chronology ends the war in 323 BC. For the fleet, Diodorus records that the Persian expedition brought about two hundred ships, with a large number of transports besides; the scale of the Greek reinforcements is exact — a hundred hoplites each from Athens and Sparta. Geographically, Pelusium lies about a hundred and sixty kilometres from Memphis in a straight line, and considerably further by the branches of the Nile; the delta itself is some two hundred kilometres from north to south and a hundred and fifty from east to west, so any expeditionary column had to be spread over several days before it could deploy in it. For order of battle, the Immortals are the core of a Persian army in Herodotus, but the number actually committed in Egypt is not recorded; the casualty figures on both sides are equally without reliable basis, and this card therefore lists no ratio of losses. The one quantifiable result is the act of sealing the river that Diodorus records: the Egyptians plugged the channel of the Nile at Pelusium with stone and timber and held the Persian fleet off outside the delta.
cause: 打起來的原因是宗主權與獨立的碰撞。埃及自阿瑪西斯二世建政以來實際獨立，卻沒有被阿契美尼德帝國正式承認為獨立國家；在波斯的編制裡，埃及自大流士一世起就是一個行省，向沙斯宮廷進貢。薩易王朝重建後的埃及國力回升：阿瑪西斯整頓了農業與灌溉、清掉孟斐斯宮廷積欠的債務、把耕地重新丈量登記，國庫充盈；三角洲的希臘僑民城市如瑙克拉里斯，把埃及與地中海世界的貿易連成一體，希臘商人、醫師與傭兵湧入孟斐斯。埃及的富庶與開放，讓波斯宮廷無法再把每年進貢視為理所當然，於是阿塔薛西斯二世在處理完王位交接與西頓、塞浦路斯方向的戰事之後，決定以武力把埃及收回行省體制。希臘城邦站在埃及一邊則是另一層原因：雅典與斯巴達都不願看到波斯獨佔尼羅河的穀物與航道，因此願意以傭兵與使節支援埃及方面的抵抗。本質上，這是一場帝國收編與區域獨立之間的正面對撞。
causeEn: The war began as a collision between a claim of overlordship and a state that had become independent. Egypt had in fact governed itself since Amasis II came to power, yet the Achaemenid Empire had never formally recognised it as an independent state: in Persian reckoning Egypt had been a satrapy since Darius I and paid tribute to Susa. The Saite kingdom had rebuilt its strength. Amasis settled the arrears of the court at Memphis, re-measured and re-registered the arable land, and left the treasury solvent; the Greek cities of the delta such as Naucratis tied Egypt into the trade of the Mediterranean, and Greek merchants, physicians and mercenaries poured into the capital. Egyptian wealth and openness made it impossible for the Persian court to treat the annual tribute as a matter of course, and so, after dealing with the succession at Susa and the wars around Sidon and Cyprus, Artaxerxes II resolved to take Egypt back into the satrapal system by force. The Greek cities took Egypt's side for a second reason: neither Athens nor Sparta wanted a single power holding the Nile's grain and its shipping lanes, and both were willing to support Egyptian resistance with mercenaries and embassies. In essence this was a head-on collision between imperial annexation and regional independence.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接後果，是埃及多保住了一段獨立的歲月。波斯兩次遠征皆無功而返，阿契美尼德帝國被迫把西征的資源轉回亞洲：往後數年，它要面對行省總督的大規模叛亂、腓尼基西頓的起義與塞浦路斯的戰事，內部的權力角力把帝國推向公元前四世紀末的崩解期。埃及這邊，阿瑪西斯解散或縮編了外來傭兵、把希臘式操練正式納入埃及軍制，國家的財政與軍力都回到可持續的軌道，首都孟斐斯重新成為地中海東岸的商業樞紐。長期看，這次勝仗只是延後了波斯解決埃及的代價：直到公元前343年阿塔薛西斯三世時代的第四次神聖戰爭，波斯才重新拿下埃及，本土王朝的獨立就此終結，埃及改為波斯行省，後來再由馬其頓人接管。希臘人與埃及的軍事往來也在此役之後更形密切，希臘式方陣與重裝步兵裝備成為埃及軍隊的骨架，影響一直延續到後來的托勒密王朝。
impactEn: The direct outcome was that Egypt bought itself a stretch of independence. Both Persian invasions failed, and the Achaemenid Empire was forced to turn its resources back towards Asia: in the years that followed it had to meet the great revolt of the satraps, the rising of Sidon in Phoenicia and the war over Cyprus, and the internal struggle for power pushed the empire towards the collapse of the late fourth century BC. In Egypt, Amasis disbanded or reduced the foreign mercenaries and folded Greek-style drill into the national army; public finances and military strength returned to a sustainable footing, and Memphis re-emerged as the commercial hinge of the eastern Mediterranean. In the long run the victory merely deferred the price Persia would pay for Egypt: only in the Fourth Sacred War of 343 BC, in the reign of Artaxerxes III, did the Persians take Egypt back, the native dynasties ended, Egypt became a Persian satrapy, and the Macedonians later inherited it. Military ties between Greeks and Egyptians also grew closer after the campaign, the Greek phalanx and the hoplite panoply becoming the skeleton of the Egyptian army — an influence that ran on into the Ptolemaic period.
result: 結果是埃及全勝。公元前358年的第一次遠征，在波斯軍剛剛進入埃及境內時便被化解，阿瑪西斯以金錢換取撤軍，雙方沒有正式交戰。公元前356年的第二次遠征規模更大，結果同樣落在埃及手上：波斯陸軍在三角洲被以長矛方陣為核心的埃及軍隊擊退，奉命封住佩盧修姆河口的埃及守軍把波斯艦隊擋在河口之外，遠征軍既不能登陸補給，也無法從陸路取得糧秣，最後沿海岸退向敘利亞。阿瑪西斯二世守住了孟斐斯與整個三角洲，埃及沒有淪為波斯行省；常見的編年把這場戰爭的下限放在公元前323年，正對應波斯徹底放棄埃及前線的時間。此後波斯王位更迭、帝國內亂，而埃及仍維持獨立法老的統治，直到公元前343年第四次神聖戰爭中敗於波斯，才把這段獨立的尾聲收掉。
resultEn: The result was an Egyptian victory. The first expedition of 358 BC was bought off shortly after it entered Egypt, Amasis paying for the withdrawal, and the two sides never fought a set-piece battle. The second expedition of 356 BC was larger, and it failed in Egypt as well: the Persian land army was repulsed in the delta by an Egyptian force built around the spear phalanx, the Egyptian garrison that sealed the mouth of the Nile at Pelusium held the Persian fleet off outside the river, and the expedition, unable either to land its supplies or to draw them overland, finally withdrew northward along the coast towards Syria. Amasis II held Memphis and the entire delta, and Egypt was not reduced to a satrapy; the usual chronology puts the end of the war in 323 BC, which corresponds to the time when Persia finally let the Egyptian front go. Thenceforward the Persian throne changed hands and the empire came apart, while Egypt went on ruling itself as an independent pharaonic kingdom, until the Fourth Sacred War of 343 BC brought Persian victory and closed that independent chapter.
